title: The data centre's crossroads
kid: Every cupboard has a road to every crossroad. Parcels spread out over all the crossroads so none gets jammed. Your parcel always takes the same crossroad, so its pieces stay in order.
nerd: ECMP gives each leaf equal-cost paths over four spines. The leaf hashes the flow's 5-tuple — source and destination IP, ports and protocol — then hash mod 4 picks spine 2. Same flow, same spine, no reordering; any leaf reaches any other in two hops.

describe.kid: At the top are four crossroads; the third is bright and named. Below are the load balancer, two other racks and the rack switch. Thin roads connect every bottom box to every crossroad. Small parcels use all roads. Your larger parcel keeps using the bright one.
describe.nerd: Four spines sit above four leaves: load balancer, two other racks and the ToR rack switch. Every leaf has a link to every spine. Background flows cross all four spines. The highlighted flow hashes to spine 2 and travels load balancer to spine to rack switch.

1995.kid: This is today’s data centre, drawn as it is now. In 1995 there was one web computer and one small hub, so there were no crossroads to choose between.
1995.nerd: Drawn as today: ECMP over a leaf–spine (Clos) fabric became the data-centre norm in the 2010s. In 1995 the web server hung off a 10 Mbit/s hub behind the site’s one router.
